content.text: Now let me validate redlines for the deviations.

input.summary: Raise cap to greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1M and subordinate it to Excluded Claims
input.comment: [Playbook] We have set the cap at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and removed "without exception" so that the Excluded Claims regime in 21.2–21.3 (confidentiality, data protection/security, indemnities, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) sits outside the cap. A one-month cap is not a meaningful remedy for a hosted service processing our data.

ops.oldText: Each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed Fees actually paid in the one month preceding the event, without exception.
ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the Fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement in the twelve months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.

input.summary: Narrow Customer indemnity and add Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity
input.comment: [Playbook] The indemnity is currently one-way. We have narrowed our indemnity to Customer-provided content and our breach of law, and added the Vendor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct — this also cures the dangling cross-references to Section 20.5 in 9.3 and 19.4.

ops.oldText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from every claim relating in any way to Customer's use of the Services.
ops.newText: 20.1 Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor from any third-party claim to the extent arising out of content or materials Customer provides to Vendor or Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

ops.text: 20.2 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The indemnified Party shall give prompt notice, allow the indemnifying Party to control the defence, and provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense; no settlement imposing an obligation on the indemnified Party is effective without its written consent.

20.5 If an infringement claim is made, Vendor shall, at its expense, procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item, or modify or replace it with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item; if neither is commercially practicable, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form and receive a refund of prepaid Fees and Fees paid for the affected item.

input.comment: [Playbook] We cannot restrict the businesses we operate or the products we build or buy, so we have deleted 12.4; it also directly contradicts 12.3. If Vendor needs protection we could look at a narrow, term-only restriction on a single named competing product with carve-outs for internal development and acquisitions.

[Playbook] We must keep the freedom to buy from other suppliers, so we have deleted the exclusivity in 2.2, which is also inconsistent with 12.3. If exclusivity is commercially important we could consider a defined category for 12 months, ending automatically if Vendor misses service levels.
